plan.title: Liver drug treatment vs control: DESeq2 DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: Design: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, raw integer gene-level counts from STAR/featureCounts (12000 genes x 6 samples), single unpaired batch. Strandedness of the library prep is not recorded in the metadata; the counting step already fixed a strand setting, so the QC step verifies it did not silently mis-assign reads before any test is trusted. The core comparison follows the standard DESeq2 count-based workflow: sample-structure QC (blinded VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to confirm treated and control separate and no sample is a covert outlier, a minimal low-count pre-filter, DESeq2's built-in median-of-ratios normalization, a Wald test on an explicit treated-vs-control contrast with an explicit reference level (control), apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control with independent filtering at alpha=0.05. Because the smallest group has only 3 replicates, statistical power is limited — this is stated explicitly in the report rather than compensated by loosening thresholds. The ranked Wald statistic from the DE step feeds a preranked fgsea analysis against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary, both available in the reference store for human) to surface coordinated pathway-level signal that individual gene calls at n=3 may miss. A final report step consolidates DE tables, fit diagnostics, p-value histogram, enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and the reproducibility record (package versions, seed, gene-set collection versions).
